gloss: small cupboard above a closet; ceiling-level storage

definitions.gloss: small cupboard near the ceiling; overhead storage above a closet
definitions.explanation: A small storage compartment built high up on the wall, typically above a Japanese-style closet (押し入れ). Found in traditional Japanese rooms, it has small sliding doors and is used for storing seldom-used items.

examples.japanese: {天袋|てんぶくろ}に{季節|きせつ}{外|はず}れの{物|もの}をしまった。
examples.english: I put out-of-season items in the overhead cupboard.

examples.japanese: {天袋|てんぶくろ}は{高|たか}すぎて{踏|ふ}み{台|だい}がないと{届|とど}かない。
examples.english: The overhead cupboard is too high to reach without a step stool.

examples.japanese: {天袋|てんぶくろ}を{開|あ}けたら、{昔|むかし}のアルバムが{出|で}てきた。
examples.english: When I opened the overhead cupboard, I found old photo albums inside.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
The {天袋|てんぶくろ} is a feature of traditional Japanese rooms ({和室|わしつ}), located above the {押|お}し{入|い}れ (closet) near the ceiling. The opposite is {地袋|じぶくろ}, a low cupboard built at floor level. Both are characteristic of Japanese domestic architecture.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {天袋|てんぶくろ}にしまう (to put away in the overhead cupboard)
- {天袋|てんぶくろ}から{出|だ}す (to take out from the overhead cupboard)
- {天袋|てんぶくろ}を{開|あ}ける (to open the overhead cupboard)

FORMS:
{天|てん} (sky, ceiling, top) + {袋|ぶくろ} (bag, pouch — here meaning enclosed storage).
